A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same GeRaF paper, with 24 readable pages including Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 2–24 are identical; first-page differences are confined to the project URL and arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on collected mmWave radar data, including reconstruction results in Table 1, novel-view synthesis in Figure 9, and ablations in Section 9.

after.justification: v2 retains the original radar reconstruction experiments, novel-view synthesis results, and ablation studies reported in v1.

M1.justification: The neural networks, physics-based RF rendering, matched filtering, lensless sampling and alpha blending, signal tracing bank, and dynamic loss masking are unchanged in Sections 4–7 and the appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same collected radar data, metal objects, line-of-sight and occluded reconstruction scenarios, and Bunny novel-view synthesis task. No dataset or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same matched-filter baseline with thresholding and Poisson surface reconstruction. No comparison method is added, removed, or revised.

E3.justification: Section 8 and Appendices C–D retain identical acquisition settings, 50,000-iteration training budget, 5,000-point mesh sampling, F1 and Chamfer-distance evaluation, and held-out novel-view setup.

E4.justification: Section 9 retains all six ablations covering scanning planes, temporal samples, positional encoding, sampling resolution, dynamic masking, and radar physics. The computational-cost analysis in Figure 7 is also unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are identical. For example, Table 1 retains Bunny F1 scores of 0.56 for MF and 0.81 for GeRaF; Figure 9 retains PSNR values of 30.5, 27.4, 29.2, and 27.9 dB.

T1.justification: The equations, computational-complexity arguments, Appendix A gradient expressions, and Appendix B derivations for lensless alpha blending and transmittance are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty and contribution claims about near-range RF geometry reconstruction, physics-based rendering, matched filtering, and efficient lensless sampling.

C2.justification: Results interpretations and limitations are identical, including Appendix E discussions of unseen surfaces, metal-only evaluation, thick occlusions, approximate reflection physics, computational cost, and multilayer surfaces.

D1.justification: The first-page project address changes from ftpsens.epfl.ch/geraf/ to sens.epfl.ch/research/geraf/. Implementation details, pseudocode, hyperparameters, and hardware disclosures remain identical; the PDFs do not establish any change in code or data availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 68 references are unchanged, including the positioning against vision-based reconstruction, far-range RF methods, and simulation-only reconstruction work.

P1.justification: Only the first-page project address and arXiv version/date text change. The title, authors, scientific prose, section order, and appendix organization remain identical.

P2.justification: The longer project URL and changed extent and placement of the marginal arXiv stamp produce limited first-page visual differences. All figures, tables, captions, and layouts on pages 2–24 render identically.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, experimental evidence, proofs, technical documentation, and limitations are identical, including the appendices. The project-address update and minor first-page presentation changes do not establish a meaningful overall quality difference; improved resource availability cannot be inferred from the PDFs.
